images.title: Three quick cases
images.purpose: Show the shortcut cases: co-prime pairs and consecutive numbers have HCF 1 and LCM the product, and for a factor and its multiple the HCF is the factor and the LCM the multiple.
images.composition: Three panels in a row, each with a small circle picture and one result line underneath, generous gaps.
exact_structure: Panel 1, heading Co-prime: a teal #0072B2 circle labelled 8 and an amber #E69F00 circle labelled 15, apart and not touching. Result line: HCF 1, LCM 120.
Panel 2, heading Factor: a small teal circle labelled 7 drawn fully inside a larger amber circle labelled 21. Result line: HCF 7, LCM 21.
Panel 3, heading Consecutive: a teal circle labelled 12 and an amber circle labelled 13, side by side and not touching. Result line: HCF 1, LCM 156.
rejection: circles overlapping in panel 1 or panel 3, or the 7 circle not inside the 21 circle
an LCM other than 120, 21 or 156, or an HCF other than 1, 7 or 1
images.takeaway: Spot co-prime, consecutive or factor pairs and write the HCF and LCM straight away.
images.description: Three panels: 8 and 15 apart give HCF 1, LCM 120; 7 inside 21 gives HCF 7, LCM 21; 12 and 13 apart give HCF 1, LCM 156.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video on tricky cases.
images.teaching_notes: Circles apart mean nothing shared, a circle inside means one number divides the other.

image_decisions.why: Seeing the three special pairs side by side helps students recognise them instantly.
